principle: The owner clarified that the supplied furniture photo is MATERIAL inspiration, NOT a template to copy. Shared identity: smoky BROWN OAK with natural open grain, polished STAINLESS STEEL accents, and solid continuous floor bases without visible legs. Vary silhouettes, door/drawer arrangements and hardware by room. REMOVE the monotonous wide horizontal metal bands of the old drawer replicas. Never turn all fronts into one repeated furniture set. No brass/gold, no orange walnut, no floating cabinets. Floor-standing cabinets have a flat continuous plinth; existing wall-mounted upper cupboards remain wall-mounted. Keep the approved white furniture, blue and small butter-yellow accents, warm stone walls, oak or appropriate wet floors, off-white curtains and existing lighting. Luxury through proportion and craft; no oversized joinery or complex new construction.

entry.name: Compact curved-front credenza
entry.design: At the EXISTING small storage location under/beyond the arch, use a narrow floor-standing oval-front brown-oak cabinet with gently rounded corners, two plain vertical-grain doors and two short vertical polished-stainless pulls. Continuous flush curved plinth, no open space or legs below. Keep the existing footprint and circulation; do not add furniture to an empty part of the entry.
entry.build: Compare a ready-made curved credenza with a shallow rectangular cabinet with radiused end panels. Confirm stair and door clearance before choosing depth.
entry.summary: A compact curved-front credenza with short vertical pulls softens the arrival area.

office.name: Architectural library wall
office.design: Retain the full north-wall TV and soundbar built-in and its existing footprint. Redesign the lower run as three tall plain slab-door bays flanking a discreet center file-drawer stack. Use vertical smoky-brown oak grain, short slim vertical stainless pulls, fine stainless shelf-edge trims on the existing open shelves, and a continuous oak toe plinth. Give the separate small printer cabinet one shallow top drawer above two doors, short horizontal stainless pulls, a flat full-width base. Keep large rectangular desk, printer and art in their current locations. NO huge horizontal metal drawer strips anywhere.
office.build: Use standard cabinet boxes with selected brown-oak slab fronts. Separate file storage, printer ventilation, TV ventilation and accessible wiring; price only selected shelf-edge metal accents.
office.summary: Slab-door library storage, selected metal-edged shelves and a smaller drawer-and-door printer cabinet give each function a clear place.

media.name: Quiet cinema console
media.design: Replace only the current long TV console with a low extra-wide three-bay brown-oak media credenza: uninterrupted plain slab end doors, a central acoustically transparent dark woven insert for equipment ventilation, and a narrow polished-stainless top-edge/recessed grip detail. Continuous full-width oak plinth, NO legs or floating unit. No broad silver stripes, no heavy fluting, no busy TV background. Keep 83-inch TV, soundbar, quiet halo panel, Cloud sectional, ceiling and rear speakers, clear west-wall doors and collectible display exactly as in target.
media.build: Use a low modular media carcass with brown-oak end doors and replaceable acoustically transparent center doors. AV installer to determine ventilation, speaker compatibility, cable paths and access.
media.summary: Plain oak doors and a ventilated woven center keep the long console quiet beneath the 83-inch screen.

bath.name: Compact framed vanity
bath.design: Redesign the existing compact vanity as a brown-oak cabinet with very thin flat frame borders around two equal DOORS, two petite polished-stainless oval pulls, white counter unchanged and a solid continuous oak plinth to the floor. Distinct from a two-drawer chest. Retain sink, toilet, doors, shower and all wet tile.
bath.build: Moisture-suitable thin-frame vanity fronts; seal edges and coordinate service access. Retain countertop and fixture positions where compatible.
bath.summary: Thin-framed oak doors and petite oval pulls create a compact vanity with a furniture-like finish.

great.name: Quiet oak door-front sideboards
great.design: Both consoles beside the fireplace should be coordinated broad low brown-oak SIDEBOARDS with three plain vertical-grain doors each, softened outside corners, paired short vertical polished-stainless pulls and one fine metal reveal beneath the top. Grounded continuous low oak plinths. No stacked drawer-chest facade and no broad metal stripes. Keep both sibling artworks above, both high windows, fireplace/TV/soundbar, stone coffee table and white Cloud seating exactly as shown.
great.build: Seek ready-made coordinated door-front sideboards on continuous bases. Coordinate dimensions to the actual fireplace-side wall widths and keep ventilation and door swings clear.
great.summary: Door-front oak sideboards with softened corners sit beneath the sibling artworks, with small vertical pulls and fine metal reveals.

kitchen.name: Tailored working kitchen
kitchen.design: Keep the kitchen layout and ivory upper cabinets. Reface visible LOWER/PANTRY cabinets in brown oak with refined narrow-frame fronts and short polished-stainless cylindrical pulls. Brown-oak island uses plain vertical-grain service drawers with slim discreet stainless edge pulls; stool-facing panel is calm broad oak panels with a recessed polished-stainless toe-kick detail. Continuous floor bases, not furniture feet. Preserve counter thickness, sink, appliances, oven column at right, island stools, pendants, windows and sunroom opening. No copied dresser-wide silver bars.
kitchen.build: Price refacing serviceable boxes. Use practical narrow-frame base doors, slab island panels and short stainless pulls; retain ivory upper cabinets to balance the darker lower joinery. Coordinate dishwasher, waste pull-outs and oven ventilation.
kitchen.summary: Tailored brown-oak lower cabinets and a slab-panel island balance the light upper cabinets, with practical short stainless pulls.

dining.name: Reeded-glass dining storage
dining.design: Long sideboard below the large artwork: four broad lightly rounded thin-frame brown-oak doors, short paired stainless pulls, fine polished-stainless top lip, solid oak plinth. The shallow storage below the center high window uses brown-oak frames with REEDED GLASS doors and slim polished-stainless vertical handles, backed by softly lit glassware shelves. Keep it below the sill. Both have flat continuous bases, no legs. No repeated horizontal metal-strip drawer chests. Keep ten-seat table, five windows, art and chandelier.
dining.build: A ready-made oak sideboard plus a shallow reeded-glass cabinet can avoid a full custom wall. Verify sill height and dining-chair pullback; use accessible low-voltage shelf lighting only if needed.
dining.summary: A quiet oak sideboard pairs with a shallow reeded-glass cabinet beneath the high window.

ownerbed.name: Soft-edged suite cabinetry
ownerbed.design: All existing bedside drawers and dressers become soft-edged smoky-brown oak pieces with radiused corners, quiet flush drawer fronts and small recessed polished-stainless finger pulls; a narrow stainless reveal only at their top edges. Bedside units have one shallow drawer over one deep drawer; the dresser uses offset wide and narrow drawer bays for useful storage, not an identical enlarged bedside chest. Continuous matching oak plinth to the floor. Keep white upholstered platform, subtle underbed lighting, low oak headwall, art, TV and soundbar, blue bedding and yellow lumbar. No broad silver stripes.
ownerbed.build: Use coordinated rounded cabinet corners and discreet stainless finger pulls. Fit actual bedside and dresser sizes around outlets and bed access; place LED channels in a serviceable recessed base only where approved.
ownerbed.summary: Rounded bedside cabinets and an offset drawer arrangement give the suite softer, individual storage pieces.

retreat.name: Hotel beverage cabinet
retreat.design: Keep the beverage-bar layout and sink/fridge positions. Lower cabinetry becomes plain flush brown-oak doors with small stainless edge pulls; one stack of narrower service drawers, full floor plinth. Upper cupboards use thin brown-oak frames with reeded glass and short vertical stainless pulls. Pale counter unchanged. In the visible adjoining bedroom repeat rounded oak nightstands with small recessed stainless finger pulls and solid floor bases, not broad metal stripes. Preserve the upholstered bench and all corner windows.
retreat.build: Reuse bar boxes and utilities where sound. Combine plain oak lower fronts and a limited pair of reeded-glass uppers; allow beverage-fridge ventilation and accessible lighting drivers.
retreat.summary: Plain oak lowers, limited reeded-glass uppers and discreet edge pulls bring a refined hotel-bar feel.

ownerbath.name: Spa vanity with vertical rhythm
ownerbath.design: Replace vanity face styling only with broad plain brown-oak doors in slender flat frames, a central narrow drawer stack, slim vertical polished-stainless pulls on doors and short horizontal pulls on drawers. Quiet evenly spaced vertical rhythm, continuous oak plinth, NO broad metal strips or floating base. Retain both sinks, pale counter, mirrors, original windows, tub artwork, shower and porcelain.
ownerbath.build: Water-resistant vanity construction with a sealed continuous base and accessible plumbing. Thin-frame doors and a central drawer bank provide variation without elaborate carved work.
ownerbath.summary: A slender frame detail, vertical door divisions and a central drawer stack create a calm spa vanity.

ownercloset.name: Functional wardrobe modules
ownercloset.design: Keep warm ivory open shelves and hanging compartments. Replace repeated dresser-looking drawer modules with brown-oak three-drawer wardrobe bases using small polished-stainless recessed cup/finger pulls and a single continuous recessed toe plinth. Add no new island or doors, preserve the aisle and clothing storage. Shelving and rods may stay as already shown.
ownercloset.build: Standard modular wardrobe carcasses with brown-oak drawer fronts and modest recessed stainless pulls. Inventory clothing before selecting drawer heights; avoid unnecessary custom curved work here.
ownercloset.summary: Practical drawer modules use modest recessed pulls within the existing light shelving system.

bed2.name: Lightly framed guest storage
bed2.design: Bedside cabinets and any dresser use crisp brown-oak THIN-FRAME faces: one slim top drawer above a single lower door, petite round polished-stainless knobs, quiet flat continuous oak bases with no feet. Brown-oak desk storage, when visible, uses the same thin-frame doors and short stainless pulls. A lighter tailored style, not rounded owner-suite pieces and not two-drawer replicas. Retain white headboard on west wall, entry position, east-window desk, blue/white bedding and yellow lumbar.
bed2.build: Choose modest thin-frame cabinet fronts and stainless knobs on grounded boxes. Retain the owner-directed layout as a site-verification item before ordering.
bed2.summary: Thin-frame doors, a shallow drawer and small round stainless knobs give this guest room a lighter character.

bed3.name: Fine vertical-texture guest storage
bed3.design: Give the bedside cabinets and dresser a restrained fine vertical-reeded BROWN OAK face on the outer door/end panels only, with smooth plain drawer fronts and small polished-stainless tab pulls. Continuous flush oak bases, NO legs, no large silver bars. Keep the texture shallow and quiet, not theatrical slats. Bed remains on right wall between windows, three windows unchanged, white bed, blue bedding and oak floor/rug unchanged.
bed3.build: Use shallow reeded veneer panels only on selected doors or end panels, with plain drawer fronts for cleaning and cost control. Match stain to the house oak sample.
bed3.summary: A little fine vertical texture on end panels contrasts with smooth drawer fronts and discreet metal tabs.

sharedbath.name: Practical twin-zone vanity
sharedbath.design: Reface the double vanity in brown oak with simple smooth slab doors beneath each sink and a central stack of three smaller drawers. Use short polished-stainless T-pulls; continuous brown-oak floor plinth. The sink bases read as doors, not repeated drawer chests. Keep both sinks, counter, mirror, lights, bathroom doors, porcelain and bedroom glimpse intact; coordinate glimpsed bedroom nightstand with fine vertical-reeded sides and small steel tab pulls.
sharedbath.build: Straight slab fronts and a central utility drawer stack can use standard boxes. Confirm traps and supply lines, moisture protection and both bedroom access routes.
sharedbath.summary: Separate sink-door bays and a central drawer stack organize the twin vanity.

laundry.name: Utility cabinetry with tailored hardware
laundry.design: Retain ivory UPPER cabinets and the exact two windows/left sink run, quote graphic and right-side washer/dryer. Reface lower run in brown oak: plain flush sink cupboard doors, one narrow drawer stack and an integrated full-height pull-out hamper with short polished-stainless bar handles. Continuous oak toe plinth, no wide metal ribbons. Preserve warm porcelain flooring and appliance service clearances.
laundry.build: Prioritize durable flat fronts and a removable integrated hamper. Brown-oak finish sample and short stainless bars unify it with the house while existing ivory uppers stay light.
laundry.summary: Plain oak sink cupboards, a narrow drawer stack and a hamper front make the utility storage practical.

loft.name: Penthouse lounge credenza and bar
loft.design: Long lounge console: brown-oak four-door credenza with a subtly rounded cabinet end, one pair of smoked-glass center doors, short polished-stainless vertical pulls and a thin silver perimeter inlay at the top; solid continuous oak plinth, no legs. Wet bar: plain oak service doors, one reeded-glass upper display and slender stainless pulls; brown-oak island face in calm broad panels. Keep all footprints, pale counters, appliances, white sectional, art, blue/yellow cushions, tray ceiling and both terrace connections. Eliminate broad horizontal drawer strips.
loft.build: Combine standard oak cabinet boxes with a small smoked-glass center section for AV and a limited reeded-glass bar display. Price curved end panels as an optional upgrade; plan ventilation, lighting access and existing bar services.
loft.summary: A softly edged oak console with smoked-glass center doors coordinates with the more detailed display bar.

bed5.name: Mitered penthouse bedroom pieces
bed5.design: Brown-oak bedside and dresser pieces with tailored MITERED box corners, plain veneer fronts and small offset polished-stainless edge pulls. Bedside: one slim drawer over an OPEN recessed book cubby, but a full-width CLOSED floor plinth below the cubby, absolutely NO feet. Dresser: three broad quiet drawers with short offset pulls. Keep the white bed, mushroom wall, blue/white bedding, yellow accent, lamps and doorway unchanged. No broad horizontal steel stripes.
bed5.build: Rectangular mitered veneer cabinets with a limited bedside book cubby, a closed plinth and replaceable short edge pulls. Keep the cubby above the base and avoid exposed feet.
bed5.summary: Mitered oak boxes, short offset pulls and bedside book cubbies give the upper guest room its own identity.

bath4.name: Compact slab-door vanity
bath4.design: Existing vanity becomes a simple plain brown-oak TWO-DOOR cabinet with long slender vertical polished-stainless pulls near the meeting stile and a continuous flush oak floor plinth. No two-drawer chest, no broad metal strips. Keep all porcelain, counter, sink, toilet, shower glass/bench and door positions exactly unchanged.
bath4.build: Standard compact two-door vanity with stain-matched oak fronts and polished-stainless pulls. Retain access for plumbing and use moisture-suitable edge sealing.
bath4.summary: Simple slab doors and slender vertical pulls suit the compact penthouse vanity.
